proved_step:
statement: For any De Morgan formula with L input-variable leaf occurrences, under a restriction in which each input variable is left live with marginal probability p, the expected number of live input-variable leaf occurrences is pL. Repeated occurrences of a variable are counted separately.
proof: For each leaf occurrence i, let I_i be 1 when its input variable is left live and 0 otherwise. The number of live input leaves is sum_{i=1}^L I_i. By linearity of expectation, its expectation is sum_i E[I_i] = sum_i p = pL. This uses only the marginal survival probability and therefore also holds under pairwise-independent restrictions.

statement: Let Phi be a De Morgan formula with L input-variable leaf occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences grouped by gate g, with f_g occurrences of g. Under any restriction distribution where each input variable is live with marginal p and each gate g is nonconstant with probability q_g, the expected number of surviving leaf occurrences is pL + sum_g f_g q_g.
proof: For every input-leaf occurrence i, define indicator I_i that its variable remains live. For every gate-leaf occurrence j of gate g, define indicator J_j that g remains nonconstant. The surviving occurrence count is sum_i I_i + sum_g sum_{j=1}^{f_g} J_j. By linearity of expectation its expectation is sum_i p + sum_g sum_j q_g = pL + sum_g f_g q_g. No independence is needed.

statement: For a finite formula with L input-leaf occurrences, let d_v be the number of occurrences of variable v. Under independent restrictions leaving each variable live with probability p, the surviving input-leaf count X satisfies E[X]=pL and Var(X)=p(1-p) sum_v d_v^2. Consequently, if every d_v<=D, Var(X)<=p(1-p)DL.
proof: Write X=sum_v d_v I_v, where I_v is the Bernoulli-p indicator that v remains live. Then E[X]=sum_v d_v p=pL. Independence gives Var(X)=sum_v d_v^2 Var(I_v)=p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2. Since d_v^2<=D d_v, summing gives sum_v d_v^2<=DL and the stated bound.

statement: Let a finite formula have input-variable leaf multiplicities d_v and L=sum_v d_v. Let I_v indicate that variable v survives a restriction, with E[I_v]=p for every v and the family (I_v) pairwise independent. For X=sum_v d_v I_v, E[X]=pL and Var(X)=p(1-p) sum_v d_v^2. Thus for every t>0, Pr(|X-pL|>=t) <= p(1-p) sum_v d_v^2/t^2; if max_v d_v<=D and L>0, then Pr(|X-pL|>=epsilon pL) <= (1-p)D/(epsilon^2 pL) for epsilon>0 and p>0.
proof: Linearity gives E[X]=sum_v d_v E[I_v]=pL. Expanding Var(X), pairwise independence implies Cov(I_u,I_v)=0 for u!=v, so Var(X)=sum_v d_v^2 Var(I_v)=p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2. Chebyshev's inequality gives the first tail bound. Under d_v<=D, sum_v d_v^2<=D sum_v d_v=DL; substituting t=epsilon pL yields the second bound.

statement: Let d_v be the input-leaf multiplicity of variable v in a finite formula, L=sum_v d_v>0, and let I_v be pairwise-independent survival indicators with common mean p>0. For X=sum_v d_v I_v, Pr(X>0) >= p^2 L^2/[p^2 L^2+p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2]. If every d_v<=D, then Pr(X>0)>=pL/[pL+(1-p)D].
proof: Because X=0 outside {X>0}, Cauchy-Schwarz gives (E X)^2=(E[X 1_{X>0}])^2<=E[X^2]Pr(X>0). Linearity gives E X=pL. Pairwise independence gives Var(X)=p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2, hence E[X^2]=p^2L^2+p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2, proving the first inequality. If d_v<=D, then sum_v d_v^2<=D sum_v d_v=DL. Substitution and cancellation of pL>0 give the second inequality.

proved_step:
statement: Let F be a finite CNF on n Boolean variables, with clauses indexed by a finite set C. For each clause C_i, let A_i be the set of assignments falsifying C_i. For S subseteq C, let N(S)=|intersection_{i in S} A_i|, with N(empty)=2^n. Then #F = sum_{S subseteq C} (-1)^|S| N(S). If each clause is a disjunction of literals, then N(S)=2^(n-|V(S)|) when the falsification requirements of all clauses in S are consistent, and N(S)=0 otherwise; here V(S) is the set of variables appearing in clauses of S.
proof: An assignment x satisfies F exactly when it lies in none of the events A_i. For each assignment x, the indicator that x lies in none of the A_i equals product_{i in C}(1-1_{A_i}(x)). Expanding the finite product gives sum_{S subseteq C}(-1)^|S| 1_{intersection_{i in S} A_i}(x). Sum over all 2^n assignments and interchange the two finite sums to obtain #F=sum_{S subseteq C}(-1)^|S|N(S). For the stated clause formula, falsifying each literal fixes its variable to one Boolean value. If two such requirements conflict on a variable then the intersection is empty. Otherwise each variable in V(S) is fixed uniquely and every variable outside V(S) is free, so the intersection has exactly 2^(n-|V(S)|) assignments. This includes S=empty by convention.

statement: Let Phi be a finite De Morgan formula whose leaves are input-variable occurrences and gate occurrences. Under a restriction, suppose each input leaf is retained with probability p and each occurrence of gate type g is retained as nonconstant with probability q_g. Let X be the number of retained leaf occurrences before simplification, and let size(Phi|rho) count leaves after restriction followed by constant folding only. If constant folding does not increase leaf count, then E[size(Phi|rho)] <= pL + sum_g f_g q_g, where L is the number of input leaves and f_g the number of occurrences of type g. Consequently, for every t>0, Pr(size(Phi|rho)>=t) <= (pL+sum_g f_g q_g)/t.
proof: Express X as the sum of indicator variables, one for each leaf occurrence. The input indicators have expectation p and each gate occurrence of type g has expectation q_g. Linearity of expectation gives E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g, with no independence assumption. By the stated constant-folding hypothesis, size(Phi|rho)<=X pointwise, so E[size(Phi|rho)]<=E[X]. Since the residual size is nonnegative, Markov's inequality gives the tail bound.

statement: Let Phi be a binary De Morgan formula with L input-leaf occurrences, each variable appearing at most once. Independently leave each variable live with probability p in [0,1], substitute constants for the other variables, and simplify constant and identity gates. Define size as leaves plus internal gates, with a constant formula of size 1. Then E[size(Phi|rho)] <= 2pL+1.
proof: Let X be the number of surviving input leaves. After simplification, either the residual is constant, of size 1, or it is a binary formula with k<=X leaves. A binary tree with k>=1 leaves has k-1 internal gates, so its size is 2k-1<=2X. Thus in either case size(Phi|rho)<=2X+1. By linearity of expectation, E[X]=pL, hence E[size(Phi|rho)]<=2pL+1.

statement: Let T be any finite rooted full binary tree with at least one leaf, and let X be its number of leaves. If size(T) counts leaves plus internal vertices, then size(T)=2X-1. Consequently, if a restriction/simplification procedure returns either a constant of size 1 or a nonconstant full binary formula R, and X is defined as the number of leaves of R (not the pre-simplification surviving-leaf count), then size(R)=1 when R is constant and size(R)=2X-1 when R is nonconstant.
proof: Let I be the number of internal vertices. Every internal vertex has exactly two children, so the number of edges is 2I. Every finite tree with I+X vertices has I+X-1 edges. Hence 2I=I+X-1, giving I=X-1 and size(T)=I+X=2X-1. The constant case follows from the stipulated size convention.

lemma: For a finite formula with input-variable leaf multiplicities d_v and L=sum_v d_v>0, under pairwise-independent variable-survival indicators I_v of common mean p>0, Pr(sum_v d_v I_v>0) >= p^2 L^2/(p^2 L^2+p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2) >= pL/(pL+(1-p)D) if max_v d_v<=D. Proof: Set X=sum_v d_v I_v. Then EX=pL and Var(X)=p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2 by pairwise independence. Thus EX^2=p^2L^2+p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2. Cauchy-Schwarz applied to X 1_{X>0} gives (EX)^2 <= EX^2 Pr(X>0), proving the first inequality. Since sum_v d_v^2<=D L, substitution and cancellation yield the second. This is only a surviving-input-leaf probability lemma; it does not bound residual formula size or prove P2'.

evidence: Pointwise injection from simplified residual leaves to surviving original nonconstant leaf occurrences; linearity of expectation. The formula Phi=x at p=N^{-a} refutes the proposed p^2 input-leaf term.
proved_step: statement: Residual-leaf charging lemma. Let Phi be a finite binary De Morgan formula tree whose leaves are input-variable occurrences and designated gate-leaf occurrences. Apply a restriction rho, substitute constants at leaves whose predicates become constant, and simplify recursively by the identities AND(0,F)=0, AND(1,F)=F, OR(1,F)=1, OR(0,F)=F. Let L be the number of input-variable leaf occurrences, and let f_g be the number of occurrences of designated gate g. If each input variable occurrence is live with marginal probability p, and each occurrence of g remains nonconstant with probability q_g, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= p L + sum_g f_g q_g, where L(Phi|rho) is the number of leaves in the simplified residual tree. Proof: Before simplification, mark each original leaf occurrence that is still nonconstant after substitution. Every leaf of the simplified tree is an original marked leaf: constant propagation deletes subtrees or replaces a parent by one child, and never creates or duplicates a leaf. Thus pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= X(rho), where X is the number of marked original leaves. By linearity of expectation, E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g; no independence is needed. Taking expectations proves the bound. The exponent-two proposal is false for Phi=x with p=N^{-a}, L=1 and no gate leaves, since its left side is p while its right side is N^{o(1)}p^2=o(p). This lemma repairs it for the exact residual-tree size, though it does not yield P2's desired shrinkage.

evidence: Complete occurrence-indicator proof is included in the statement. This is a repaired leaf-level estimate with linear survival probabilities; it does not prove P2' for residual formula size.
proved_step: statement: Let Phi be a finite formula whose leaves are occurrences indexed by k in a finite set K. Under a random restriction, let I_k be the indicator that occurrence k remains a leaf before constant folding, and set r_k=Pr[I_k=1]. Suppose the residual-size convention counts leaves after constant folding and that this folding never increases the leaf count. Then E[|Phi|_res] <= sum_{k in K} r_k, and for every t>0, Pr(|Phi|_res >= t) <= (sum_{k in K} r_k)/t. Proof: pointwise, |Phi|_res <= sum_k I_k by the nonincrease assumption. Taking expectations and using linearity gives E|Phi|_res <= sum_k E I_k = sum_k r_k, without any independence assumption. Markov's inequality for the nonnegative random variable |Phi|_res gives the tail bound.

statement: Let N>1, let L be the number of input-variable leaf occurrences of a De Morgan formula, and let p=p(N) satisfy p(N)=N^{-epsilon(N)} for some epsilon(N)->0. Under any restriction distribution in which each input variable is live with marginal probability p, the expected number of surviving input-variable leaf occurrences is at most N^{epsilon(N)} p^2 L. Proof: For each occurrence i let I_i be its survival indicator and X=sum_i I_i. By linearity E[X]=pL. Since p=N^{-epsilon(N)}, pL=N^{epsilon(N)}p^2L exactly. No independence assumption is needed. Thus, on the restricted regime p=N^{-o(1)}, the input-leaf contribution to P2' is absorbed by its proposed p^2L term with an explicit subpolynomial factor; this does not control gate-leaf contributions or prove P2'.

statement: Let T be a finite rooted binary formula tree whose leaves are partitioned into input-variable occurrences and gate occurrences. Under a restriction, each input occurrence survives as a variable with marginal probability p, and each occurrence of gate g remains nonconstant with marginal probability q_g. Define the residual tree by replacing every non-surviving leaf by a Boolean constant, evaluating constant subtrees, and suppressing unary internal nodes without duplicating subtrees; count one node for a constant. If T has L input leaves and f_g occurrences of g, then E[size(T|rho)] <= 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g)+1. Proof: Let X count the surviving nonconstant leaves. Indicator variables and linearity of expectation give E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g. If X=0, the residual is a constant of size one. If X>0, any subtree with no surviving nonconstant leaf evaluates to a constant and is collapsed, so every residual leaf descends from one of the X surviving leaves. The residual tree therefore has at most X leaves. A binary tree with t leaves has t-1 internal nodes, hence size at most 2X-1 when X>0. In either case size <=2X+1; taking expectations proves the claim. This repairs the squared-probability target to a linear-probability bound under the stated semantics; it does not establish compatibility with the dossier's intended size measure.

statement: Let T be a finite De Morgan formula tree over literals and constants, with input-variable leaf occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences. Fix a restriction and mark as active each input occurrence whose variable remains live and each gate occurrence whose restricted gate is nonconstant; let X be the number of active occurrences. Simplify T recursively using De Morgan gates: evaluate constant gates, use x AND 1=x, x AND 0=0, x OR 0=x, x OR 1=1 and their dual/complement forms, and suppress unary nodes; never duplicate a subtree. Then the resulting formula has at most X nonconstant leaves, and its node count is at most 2X+1. Consequently, for random restrictions with marginal live probability p on each input variable occurrence and marginal nonconstant probability q_g on each occurrence of gate g, E[size(T|rho)] <= 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g)+1. Proof: By recursive simplification, every residual subtree either is constant or computes a nonconstant function that depends on at least one active leaf below it. In a residual tree that is not constant, every leaf is nonconstant: a constant child of an AND/OR gate either makes the parent constant or is removed by the neutral-element rule, and the same holds for complemented De Morgan forms. Hence every residual leaf is descended from an active occurrence, so the residual has at most X leaves. A binary tree with t leaves has t-1 internal nodes, giving at most 2X-1 nodes when nonconstant; if constant, it has one node. Thus size <=2X+1. Indicator linearity gives E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g, proving the expectation bound. This conclusion depends on full constant/neutral-element simplification; the weaker rule in S0013 that only evaluates constant subtrees is insufficient (e.g. (x AND 1) AND 1 can retain two constant leaves when x is active).

statement: Let Phi be a finite formula whose residual size after restriction is defined syntactically, before Boolean simplification, by counting each surviving input-variable leaf occurrence once and replacing every non-surviving input leaf by a constant. If Phi has L input-variable leaf occurrences and each underlying variable is live with marginal probability p, then E[L(Phi|rho)] = pL. Consequently, for Phi=x, p=N^{-alpha} with any fixed alpha>0, and any prefactor a(N)=N^{o(1)}, the bound E[L(Phi|rho)] <= a(N)p^2 L fails for all sufficiently large N.
proof: For each leaf occurrence i, define I_i(rho)=1 when its variable is live and 0 otherwise. By the stipulated syntactic size convention, L(Phi|rho)=sum_{i=1}^L I_i(rho). Therefore linearity of expectation gives E[L(Phi|rho)]=sum_i E[I_i]=pL; no independence is needed. For Phi=x, L=1 and p=N^{-alpha}, so the proposed right side is a(N)N^{-2alpha}, whereas the left side is N^{-alpha}. Since a(N)=N^{o(1)}, the ratio of left to right is N^{alpha-o(1)}, which tends to infinity; thus the inequality fails eventually. The single-variable restriction distribution is pairwise independent vacuously.
scope: Syntactic residual leaf count before Boolean simplification; any finite formula for the equality, and the single-leaf formula for the asymptotic counterexample. This does not address residual size after Boolean simplification.

statement: For a binary De Morgan formula with L variable-leaf occurrences, let X be the number left live by a restriction. Substitute constants, then recursively eliminate every AND/OR gate with a constant child by its Boolean identity. The residual node count is at most 2X+1. If each variable is live with marginal p, its expected node count is at most 2pL+1.
proof: The simplification duplicates no subtree. If the output is constant, size is 1. Otherwise every leaf is a live variable and every internal node has two children. If there are X' leaves, then X'<=X and a finite full binary tree has X'-1 internal nodes; total size is 2X'-1<=2X+1. Also X is the sum of L occurrence indicators of mean p, so E[X]=pL by linearity. Taking expectations proves the expectation bound.
scope: Binary formula; total node count; exactly the recursive constant simplification stated.

evidence: This proves a weaker linear-survival residual-size bound from the exact leaf-survival marginals. It does not prove heterogeneous P2', whose right side uses p^2 L and sum_g f_g q_g^2. For the single input leaf formula Phi=x with survival probability 0<p<1, E[X]=p while p^2 L=p^2, so the proposed squared input term does not follow from marginal survival alone.
proved_step: statement: Let T be a finite binary De Morgan formula tree whose leaves consist of ordinary input-variable occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences. Under any restriction, suppose each leaf occurrence is either replaced by a Boolean constant or remains as one nonconstant leaf, and simplification repeatedly deletes a constant child using the Boolean identities for AND and OR, without expanding or duplicating any surviving leaf. Let X be the number of surviving leaf occurrences. Then the simplified residual has at most 2X+1 nodes. If input leaf i survives with probability p_i and gate leaf j survives with probability q_j, its expected node count is at most 2(sum_i p_i + sum_j q_j)+1. Proof: the simplification preserves the binary-tree property and never duplicates leaves. If the output is constant, it has one node. Otherwise all remaining leaves are among the X surviving occurrences, so their number X' is at most X. In any finite full binary tree with X' leaves, the number of internal nodes is X'-1, hence total nodes are 2X'-1 <= 2X+1. Taking expectations and applying linearity to X gives E[X]=sum_i p_i+sum_j q_j, without any independence assumption; therefore E[nodes] <= 2E[X]+1. Scope is only the stated constant-simplification model and total node count.

statement: Let Phi be a finite De Morgan formula with L input-leaf occurrences, and let rho be any distribution of restrictions such that every input variable is live with marginal probability p. Form Phi|rho by substituting constants for fixed variables and simplifying constants by De Morgan constant folding, without duplicating subformulas. Count only nonconstant variable-leaf occurrences in the simplified residual. Then E[L_var(Phi|rho)] <= pL.
proof: For each original input-leaf occurrence i, let I_i be 1 if its variable is live under rho. Before simplification the number of nonconstant variable-leaf occurrences is exactly X=sum_i I_i. Constant folding at AND/OR/NOT nodes deletes or retains subtrees and never duplicates a leaf occurrence, so L_var(Phi|rho)<=X for every restriction. Taking expectations and using E[I_i]=p gives E[L_var(Phi|rho)]<=E[X]=sum_i p=pL. No independence assumption is needed. This repairs only the input-leaf term under the stated simplification semantics; it does not bound residual gate-leaves or establish P2'.

statement: Let T be a finite rooted Boolean formula tree whose leaves are input variables, and let rho be any partial assignment to those variables. Define T|rho recursively by substituting fixed leaves by constants and simplifying each AND/OR node by the identities 0 AND A=0, 1 AND A=A, 0 OR A=A, 1 OR A=1; whenever a gate becomes a constant or has one surviving child, replace that subtree by its resulting constant or child. Then the number of variable-leaf occurrences in T|rho is at most the number of leaves of T whose variables are left unassigned by rho.
Proof: Induct on T. For a variable leaf, its restricted residual has zero variable leaves if fixed and one if live, matching the live-leaf count. Suppose T is an AND or OR node with children T1,T2. By induction, each simplified child has at most as many variable leaves as the live leaves in its original child. Before final gate simplification, the combined tree therefore has at most the sum of those bounds, which is the live-leaf count in T. Each listed simplification either replaces a subtree by a constant or deletes a gate while retaining a child; neither increases variable-leaf count. Thus the final residual obeys the bound. This result concerns only tree syntax with variable leaves; it does not cover shared/reused gate leaves or arbitrary residual-size measures.

statement: For every sufficiently large N, set p=N^{-1/3} and let Phi be the one-leaf De Morgan formula x. Under the restriction that leaves x live with probability p, E[L(Phi|rho)] is at least p, so no bound E[L(Phi|rho)] <= N^{o(1)} p^2 can hold uniformly over such formulas and restrictions, when N^{o(1)} denotes a subpolynomial factor.
proof: There are no gate leaves, so the proposed right side is N^{o(1)}p^2. If x is live, Phi|rho=x and has one input leaf; otherwise its residual is constant and has nonnegative size. Therefore E[L(Phi|rho)] >= Pr[x is live]=p=N^{-1/3}. For every subpolynomial factor N^{o(1)}=N^{epsilon(N)} with epsilon(N)->0, the proposed upper bound is N^{-2/3+epsilon(N)}, which is strictly less than N^{-1/3} for all sufficiently large N. The one-coordinate survival family is pairwise independent vacuously. Hence the universal P2' inequality is refuted in this model.

statement: Let Φ be a finite De Morgan formula with input-variable leaf occurrences of total count L and gate-leaf occurrences grouped by gates g, with f_g occurrences of g. Apply any restriction under which each input variable is live with marginal probability p and each gate g is nonconstant with probability q_g. Form Φ|ρ by substituting constants for restricted inputs and constant gates, then only applying constant folding that never duplicates nodes. If L(·) counts leaf occurrences, then E[L(Φ|ρ)] ≤ pL + Σ_g f_g q_g. No independence assumptions are required.
proof: For each original input-leaf occurrence i, let I_i indicate that its variable is live. For each original gate-leaf occurrence j labelled g, let J_j indicate that g is nonconstant. Before constant folding, the restricted syntax has exactly Σ_i I_i + Σ_g Σ_{j=1}^{f_g} J_j surviving leaf occurrences. Constant folding that never duplicates nodes cannot increase this count, so pointwise L(Φ|ρ) ≤ Σ_i I_i + Σ_g Σ_j J_j. Taking expectations and using linearity gives E[L(Φ|ρ)] ≤ Σ_i Pr(I_i=1) + Σ_g Σ_j Pr(J_j=1) = pL + Σ_g f_g q_g. Correlations among survival events do not affect this calculation. This repairs the input contribution in P2′, but does not establish the proposed squared-probability gate contribution or any stronger shrinkage bound.

evidence: The proof uses pairwise independence gate-by-gate: a surviving-nontrivial gate requires at least one live pair in its support, and each such pair is live with probability p^2. Experiment cm-72d0e7a1a7a54563 finitely corroborated the bound on unbiased linear-form families over F2 for d<=8. The experiment is not the proof. Scope: common marginal p and the explicit >=2-live-support definition.
proved_step: statement: Let U be a finite set of variables and let I_v in {0,1} indicate whether v remains live under a random restriction. Assume E[I_v]=p for all v and the indicators are pairwise independent. For any finite family G of Boolean functions g, let supp(g) subseteq U have size d_g and assume g depends only on supp(g). Define g to survive nontrivially when at least two variables in supp(g) remain live. Then Pr[g survives nontrivially] <= min(1, binom(d_g,2)p^2). Consequently, for any nonnegative occurrence weights f_g, E[sum_{g in G} f_g 1(g survives nontrivially)] <= sum_{g in G} f_g min(1, binom(d_g,2)p^2). Proof: If g has fewer than two live support variables, its restricted function depends on at most one variable and is therefore constant or a literal (possibly negated), so it is not nontrivial by definition. Thus the event that g survives nontrivially is contained in the union over unordered pairs {u,v} subseteq supp(g) of events {I_u=I_v=1}. Pairwise independence and the common marginal give Pr[I_u=I_v=1]=p^2 for each pair. The union bound gives Pr[g survives] <= binom(d_g,2)p^2, and every probability is at most 1, yielding the minimum. Multiply by f_g and sum; linearity of expectation yields the consequence without independence between different gates.

statement: Let Phi be a De Morgan formula with L input-leaf occurrences, no gate-leaves, and no variable appearing more than once. Independently leave each variable live with probability p and assign every other variable a Boolean constant. After constant propagation and Boolean simplification, let L_res be the number of live input-leaf occurrences remaining. Then E[L_res] <= pL.
proof: For each original input-leaf occurrence i let I_i indicate that its variable is live. Restriction replaces leaves only by constants, and Boolean simplification cannot introduce a new input-variable occurrence. Hence pointwise L_res <= sum_{i=1}^L I_i. By linearity of expectation, E[sum_i I_i]=sum_i p=pL, proving the claim.
gap: P2' input-leaf contribution under an explicit read-once, no-gate-leaf restriction; this does not establish the general P2' residual-size bound.

evidence: The proof correctly bounds residual size by 2X+1 where X counts surviving nonconstant leaves. Linearity of expectation gives E[X] = pL + sum f_g q_g. The bound is linear in probabilities, not quadratic. The caveat about the dossier's size measure is noted.

Stronger simplification (full constant/neutral-element rules) correctly yields at most X nonconstant leaves. The counterexample to S0013's weaker rule is valid: (x AND 1) AND 1 with x active retains two constant-1 leaves under only constant-subtree evaluation. Proof is sound.

Correct: syntactic leaf count L(Phi|rho) = sum I_i, so E[L] = pL exactly. For Phi=x, L=1, p=N^{-alpha}, left side = N^{-alpha}, right side = a(N)N^{-2alpha} = N^{-2alpha+o(1)}. Ratio = N^{alpha-o(1)} -> infinity. Valid counterexample to quadratic bound under syntactic measure.

Correct: recursive constant simplification without duplication gives size <= 2X+1. X = sum of L indicators, E[X] = pL. Bound holds. This matches S0013/S0014 but with explicit 'no duplication' condition.

Checked the argument line by line: (i) constant-simplification preserves the binary tree property and never duplicates a leaf, since it only replaces a node by a constant or deletes a parent gate while keeping one child; (ii) if the residual is nonconstant then every residual leaf is one of the X surviving occurrences, X' <= X; (iii) a full binary tree with X' leaves has X'-1 internal nodes so nodes = 2X'-1 <= 2X+1, and a constant residual has size 1 <= 2X+1; (iv) E[X] = sum_i p_i + sum_j q_j by linearity alone, no independence needed. So the heterogeneous per-occurrence survival bound is correct. As the step's own evidence note says, it does NOT give the squared p^2 / q_g^2 target, and the single-leaf instance Phi=x (E[X]=p, p^2 L = p^2) blocks any derivation of that from marginals alone.

Variables: before folding, the number of nonconstant variable-leaf occurrences is exactly X = sum_i I_i, so L_var <= X pointwise because De Morgan constant folding only deletes/keeps subtrees and never duplicates a leaf occurrence. E[I_i] = p for every occurrence by the marginal hypothesis, so E[L_var] <= pL with no independence assumption and no constraint on the joint law of rho. Correct as stated; scoped to input leaves only (a duplicate of the input term of S0017, correctly carved out).

Induction on T checked. Variable leaf: 0 residual leaves if fixed, 1 if live — matches the live-leaf count. AND/OR node: by IH the simplified children have at most the live-leaf counts of their originals, so the pre-simplification tree has at most the live count of T; every listed identity (0 AND A=0, 1 AND A=A, 0 OR A=A, 1 OR A=1) either replaces a subtree by a constant or deletes a gate keeping a child, never adding a variable leaf. Hence the final residual's variable-leaf count is at most the number of leaves left unassigned. Valid; the stated restriction to tree syntax (no shared subformulas) is exactly what the induction needs and is honestly flagged.

Arithmetic verified: with L=1, if x is live (prob p=N^{-1/3}) the residual is x with one input leaf, otherwise a constant; so E[L(Phi|rho)] >= p = N^{-1/3}. The proposed bound is N^{o(1)}p^2 = N^{-2/3+eps(N)} with eps(N)->0, and N^{-2/3+eps(N)}/N^{-1/3} = N^{-1/3+eps(N)} -> 0, so the bound fails for all large N. statement: Let Phi be a finite full binary De Morgan formula tree with input-variable leaf occurrences and designated gate-leaf occurrences. Under a restriction, substitute constants for leaves whose predicates become constant and simplify by the usual constant-folding identities, without introducing or duplicating leaves. Let X be the number of original leaf occurrences that remain nonconstant before folding, with E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g, where L is the number of input-variable occurrences and f_g is the number of occurrences of gate g. If the residual is nonconstant, it is a finite full binary tree, so its number of internal vertices is Y-1 and its total size is 2Y-1 <= 2X+1. If it is constant, its size is 1 <= 2X+1. statement: Heterogeneous pair bound: Let U be finite, let (I_v)_{v in U} be pairwise-independent {0,1}-valued indicators with Pr[I_v=1]=p_v, and let each Boolean function g depend only on S_g subseteq U. Hence for nonnegative occurrence weights f_g, E[sum_g f_g 1(g survives nontrivially)] <= sum_g f_g min(1, sum_{ {u,v} subseteq S_g } p_u p_v). Proof: the event of at least two live support variables is contained in the union of pair-live events; pairwise independence gives each event probability p_u p_v; apply the union bound and cap by one. Multiply by f_g and sum by linearity of expectation.

With A=(1+p)/2, the sums of k binom(L,k) p^k 2^(-(L-k)) and binom(L,k) p^k 2^(-(L-k)) over k>=1 are respectively Lp A^(L-1) and A^L-2^(-L), yielding the formula.

statement: Residual-leaf charging lemma (linear form). Let Phi be a finite binary De Morgan formula tree. Its leaves are either input-variable occurrences or designated gate occurrences indexed by g; let L be the number of input-variable occurrences and f_g the number of occurrences of gate g. Apply a restriction rho, replace each restricted leaf by its resulting constant when it becomes constant, and recursively simplify by constant propagation, suppressing unary nodes and never duplicating a subtree. Let R(Phi,rho) be the resulting formula and count its leaves, including a single leaf if it is constant. Suppose each input-variable occurrence is nonconstant after substitution with probability p, and each occurrence of gate g is nonconstant with probability q_g. Then E[leaves(R(Phi,rho))] <= pL + sum_g f_g q_g. No independence assumption is required.
Proof. For a fixed rho, mark each original leaf occurrence that remains nonconstant after substitution, and let X(rho) be the number of marked leaves. Recursive simplification only deletes subtrees, replaces a parent by one of its existing children, or returns a constant; by hypothesis it never duplicates a subtree. Thus every nonconstant leaf of the simplified formula is an original marked leaf. If simplification returns a constant, its one leaf is also bounded by X unless X=0; in that case the original formula has no nonconstant leaves, so the simplified constant has one leaf. To avoid this exceptional additive constant, use the stated convention that a constant output has zero residual leaves for this lemma. Under that convention, pointwise leaves(R) <= X. By linearity of expectation, E[X] is the sum of the survival probabilities over occurrences, namely pL + sum_g f_g q_g. Taking expectations proves the bound.
Scope. This is a linear bound for residual leaves under the zero-leaf convention for constants. It does not prove a quadratic P2' bound. If constants are instead counted as one leaf, the same proof gives E[leaves(R)] <= pL + sum_g f_g q_g + Pr[R is constant].

statement: Read-once residual-size lemma (Boolean De Morgan formulas). Let T be a finite binary De Morgan formula tree whose leaves are distinct input variables, with no designated reused-gate leaves. Let rho be any random restriction; each variable v is live with marginal probability p_v. Define T|rho by substituting fixed bits and recursively simplifying constants, counting a constant output as size 1 and otherwise counting all leaves and internal nodes. Then E[size(T|rho)] <= 2 sum_v p_v + 1. In the common-marginal case p_v=p with L leaves, E[size(T|rho)] <= 2pL+1.
proof: For each restriction outcome, let X be the number of original variable leaves that are live. Recursive constant folding and unary-node suppression never creates or duplicates leaves. Thus each nonconstant residual leaf descends from a distinct live original leaf, so the residual leaf count Y is at most X. If the residual output is nonconstant, it is a full binary tree; with Y leaves it has Y-1 internal nodes, hence size 2Y-1. If the output is constant, its size is 1. In either case size(T|rho) <= 2Y+1 <= 2X+1. Taking expectations and using linearity, E[size] <= 2E[X]+1 = 2 sum_v p_v+1. No independence assumption is needed. This proves a linear-in-survival-probability residual-size bound for read-once formulas; it does not prove quadratic heterogeneous P2' for formulas with reused gate leaves.

statement: Let Phi be a finite binary formula tree whose leaves are input-variable occurrences or designated gate-leaf occurrences. Define residual size after constant folding and unary-node suppression as the number of leaves plus internal nodes, with a constant output having size 1. A nonconstant binary residual tree with Y leaves has 2Y-1 nodes; a constant residual has size 1. Thus pointwise size(Phi|rho) <= 2X+1. For Phi=x and p=N^-a, a>0, the proposed P2' quadratic input term N^{o(1)}p^2 is o(p), whereas expected residual leaf count is p, so this repaired linear bound does not imply P2'.

Proof: Independence gives E[2^K]=prod_i E[2^{I_i}]=(1+p)^d. The K=0 term contributes (1-p)^d and the K=1 terms contribute dp(1-p)^{d-1}; however the displayed identity as written subtracts 1+dp, so it is not the claimed expectation. The exact expectation is (1+p)^d-(1-p)^d-dp(1-p)^{d-1}. For dp<=1, use 2^K 1(K>=2) <= 2^K-1-K, so its expectation is at most (1+p)^d-1-dp <= (e/2)(dp)^2, since (1+p)^d <= e^{dp} and e^x-1-x <= (e/2)x^2 for 0<=x<=1.

statement: Let I_1,...,I_d be mutually independent Bernoulli(p) variables, K=sum_i I_i, and dp<=1. Then E[2^K 1(K>=2)] <= 2e(dp)^2. Proof: For integer k=0,1 both sides of 2^k 1(k>=2)<=4(2^k-1-k) vanish. For k>=2, this inequality is equivalent to 3*2^k-4k-4>=0; equality holds at k=2 and the expression increases thereafter since its increment is 3*2^k-4>0. Thus the expectation is at most 4(E[2^K]-1-E[K])=4((1+p)^d-1-dp), by independence. Put x=dp<=1. Since (1+p)^d<=e^x and e^x-1-x<=e*x^2/2 on [0,1] by Taylor's theorem, the result follows.

statement: Let I_1,...,I_d be mutually independent Bernoulli(p) variables, K=sum_i I_i, and dp<=1. Then E[2^K 1(K>=2)] <= 2e(dp)^2. Taking expectations and using independence gives E[2^K 1(K>=2)] <= 4(E[2^K]-1-E[K])=4((1+p)^d-1-dp). Set x=dp. Since (1+p)^d<=e^x and, by Taylor's theorem, e^x-1-x<=e*x^2/2 for 0<=x<=1, the claimed bound follows.

Witnessed-leaf bound. Let I be a finite set of counted leaf occurrences. For each i∈I choose two distinct variables x_i,w_i and an event A_i implying that both x_i and w_i survive a restriction. If the survival indicators of distinct variables are pairwise independent and each has marginal p, then E[|{i∈I:A_i}|] ≤ |I|p². Proof: for each i, 1_{A_i}≤1_{x_i survives}1_{w_i survives}; the two indicators are independent, so Pr(A_i)≤p². Sum these inequalities by linearity of expectation. Thus the P2′ input-leaf term holds for any subclass where every residual counted input leaf has such a distinct-witness necessity condition, with no independence assumption between different leaf events.

Then E[size(Phi|rho)] <= 1 + 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g). Proof: Let X be the number of original occurrences that remain nonconstant before folding. statement: Let T be a finite rooted full binary De Morgan formula tree with input-variable leaves and designated-gate leaves. Under a restriction, suppose constant folding yields either a constant or a full binary tree, and every leaf of a nonconstant residual tree traces to a distinct original leaf occurrence that remained nonconstant. If each input occurrence survives with probability p and each occurrence of gate g survives with probability q_g, then E[size(T|rho)] <= 1 + 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g), where size counts all vertices and a constant has size 1.

statement: Two-stage survival repair. Let T be a finite formula tree with L input-leaf occurrences and f_g occurrences of each designated gate g. For each occurrence e, let A_e and B_e be events, and retain e exactly when both occur. Suppose Pr(A_e)=a_e, Pr(B_e)=b_e, and A_e,B_e are independent for that occurrence. After retaining leaves and applying only constant folding that never duplicates leaves, the residual leaf count R satisfies E[R] <= sum_e a_e b_e. In particular, if input occurrences have a_e=b_e=p and gate occurrences labelled g have a_e=b_e=q_g, then E[R] <= p^2 L + sum_g f_g q_g^2. Proof: Set I_e=1 when both required events occur. Independence gives E[I_e]=a_e b_e. Constant folding cannot create or duplicate leaves, so pointwise R <= sum_e I_e. Taking expectations and using linearity proves the bound; distinct occurrences need not be independent. This repairs the marginal-survival obstruction only for a two-stage survival mechanism. It does not establish that the CLOSURE-B restriction has such a mechanism or that its P2' RHS has the N^{o(1)} factor.
proof: For each original leaf occurrence e, define I_e to be 1 exactly when both of its required survival events occur. By the stipulated within-occurrence independence, E[I_e]=Pr(A_e and B_e)=a_e b_e. statement: Influence-edge restriction bound. Let g:{0,1}^d->{0,1}. Independently for each coordinate j, leave j live with probability p and otherwise fix it to a uniform bit. Let E_i(g) be the set of unordered edges of the d-cube in direction i on which g changes. Then Pr[g restricted by rho is nonconstant] <= p * sum_{i=1}^d |E_i(g)| * ((1+p)/2)^(d-1).
